title: Customer Count by Country
description:
Count how many customers are from each country. Return the country and the count.

**Table: customers**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| email | VARCHAR |
| city | VARCHAR |
| country | VARCHAR |

Output columns: `country`, `customer_count`. Order by `customer_count` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'alice@example.com', 'New York', 'USA'), (2, 'Bob', 'bob@example.com', 'London', 'UK'), (3, 'Carol', 'carol@example.com', 'Chicago', 'USA'), (4, 'Dan', 'dan@example.com', 'Mumbai', 'India'), (5, 'Eve', 'eve@example.com', 'Los Angeles', 'USA'), (6, 'Fay', 'fay@example.com', 'Manchester', 'UK');
solution_sql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY customer_count DESC
hints: GROUP BY country collapses all rows for the same country into one.
COUNT(*) counts the number of rows in each group.
explanation: `GROUP BY country` creates one group per country. `COUNT(*)` counts the rows in each group. The result is ordered by count descending so the most-represented country appears first.
